title: CROWDGUARD v2.0 Live Monitoring & Incident Lifecycle Validation

validation_stages.name: Pipeline Data-Flow & Component Coupling
validation_stages.description: Verifies data flows seamlessly from detection/speed/flow metrics into risk engine and alert evaluator.
validation_stages.limitations: Evaluates simulated numerical tensor outputs rather than physical optical photons.

validation_stages.name: Alert Sustenance Window & Flicker Suppression (N=3 Frames)
validation_stages.description: Requires condition to sustain for 3 consecutive frames before firing. Suppresses transient single-frame spikes.
validation_stages.limitations: Introduces ~2-3 frame latency (~0.2-0.3s at 10 FPS) before alert generation to confirm hazard validity.

validation_stages.name: Cooldown Window & Duplicate Incident Prevention
validation_stages.description: Verifies that an ongoing elevated hazard does not spam duplicate incident records during the 4.0s cooldown window, but re-triggers if hazard persists past cooldown.
validation_stages.limitations: Rapidly fluctuating hazards near the cooldown boundary could generate spaced repeat records.

validation_stages.name: Condition De-escalation & State Counter Reset
validation_stages.description: Verifies condition counter immediately clears to 0 when crowd metrics normalize, preventing historical accumulation.
validation_stages.limitations: Requires at least 1 normalized frame to reset; single dropped frame from camera does not automatically reset.

validation_stages.name: Incident Lifecycle State Machine (Open -> Acknowledged -> Resolved)
validation_stages.description: Verifies complete operator incident workflow transitions from initial Open, operator Acknowledged, to Resolved with audit notes.
validation_stages.limitations: Audit trail is stored in operator_notes string; full multi-user audit logging table not yet configured.

validation_stages.name: Evidence Snapshot Integrity & Retrieval
validation_stages.description: Verifies keyframe evidence snapshot is generated, saved to filesystem, and retrieved cleanly with correct dimensions.
validation_stages.limitations: Evidence snapshots are stored as individual JPEG files on local disk; no object storage / S3 integration.

validation_stages.name: Timestamp Traceability & Monotonicity Ordering
validation_stages.description: Verifies strict time ordering across capture, inference, risk evaluation, alert emission, and record persistence.
validation_stages.limitations: Cross-clock domain comparisons (wall clock vs monotonic) can have minor sub-millisecond NTP drift.

validation_stages.name: Camera Disconnection & Stale Telemetry Protection
validation_stages.description: Verifies disconnected camera marks telemetry as stale (is_stale=True), preventing downstream systems from assuming safe zero-risk, and reconnects with clean state buffers.
validation_stages.limitations: Stale telemetry is preserved in memory for operator reference until stream re-establishes.

validation_stages.name: Multi-Camera Alert & Incident Isolation
validation_stages.description: Verifies independent camera streams maintain strict alert isolation. Critical hazard on Cam A creates zero incidents for Cam B.
validation_stages.limitations: Does not perform automated correlation of incidents across adjacent cameras covering the same venue.

validation_stages.name: End-to-End Alert Decision Latency (25 Iterations)
validation_stages.description: Measures CPU execution time required to evaluate sustenance window, verify cooldowns, and instantiate alert object.
validation_stages.limitations: Excludes disk I/O when persistence is deferred; SQLite transaction overhead adds ~2-5ms when writing to database.

architecture_summary.pipeline_sequence: Ingestion -> Person Detection -> ByteTrack -> Spatial Grid -> Risk Engine -> Sustained Alert Evaluator -> Incident Persistence -> Operator HUD

scientific_disclaimer: Scientific Integrity Disclaimer: Generated incidents and alerts represent heuristic decision-support warnings synthesized from DIP and computer vision features for operator guidance. They do not constitute autonomous life-safety actuation or guaranteed disaster predictions.
